title.narrative: Indonesia Second Power Transmission Development Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Power Transmission Development Project for Indonesia is to meet growing electricity demand and increase access to electricity in the project area through strengthening and expanding the capacity of the power transmission networks in the project area in a sustainable manner. The project has single component with following two parts: first part is extension and rehabilitation of selected existing 150-20 Kilovolt (kV) substations and 70-20 kV substations in the project area, including adding one or more new transformers and associated equipment; and or replacing existing transformers with new transformers and associated equipment with higher capacity; and second part is construction of selected new 150-20 kV substations in the project area, including installation of transformers and associated equipment.

The development objective of the project is to meet growing electricity demand in the Project Area through strengthening and expanding the capacity of the power transmission networks in the Project Area in a sustainable manner.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :Loan Agreement Section 5.01 | Description :The Additional Conditions of Effectiveness consists of the following,namely that the Subsidiary Loan Agreement has been executed on behalf of the Borrower and the Project Implementing Entity. | DueDate :26-Nov-2013

Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section I.A 6 | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall appoint a projectmanagement consultant one month after the Effectiveness Date and thereaftermaintain throughout the Project. | Due Date :28-Apr-2014

Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section I.B.3(a) | Description :All Sub-projects need to meet the EligibilityCriteria described in the Project Agreement and Project Implementation Plan | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section I.B.3(b) | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall provide to theBank the Project Implementing Entity's rolling investment plan, including those activities that constitute proposed Group 2Sub-projects no later than January 15 in each year of Project implementation. | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section I.D | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall carry out theProject in accordance with the safeguard instruments listed in the Project Agreement, including the specific provisions toEnvironmental Management Plans, to Land Acquisition and Resettlement and to Indigenous People | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section II.A | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall monitor andevaluate the progress of the Project and prepare Project Report. Each such report shall cover the period of one calendar year, andshall be furnished to the Bank no later than forty five days after the end of the period covered by such report. | Frequency:Yearly

Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section II.B.2 | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall prepare andfurnish to the Bank, interim un-audited financial reports for the Project covering the preceding quarter, in form and substancesatisfactory to the Borrower and the Bank no later than forty five days after the endof each calendar quarter. | Frequency:Quarterly

Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section II.B.3 | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall have itsfinancial statements audited by independent auditors acceptable to the Borrower and the Bank, in accordance with consistentlyapplied auditing standards acceptable to the Borrower and the Bank. Each such audit shall cover one fiscal year of the ProjectImplementing Entity and be submitted to the Bank no later than 6 months after the end of the period. | Frequency :Yearly
Finance Agreement :Project Agreement Schedule Section II.B.4 | Description :The Project Implementing Entity shall maintain a debtservice coverage ratio of 1.5 times. | Frequency :Yearly

title.narrative: Commissioned capacity of transformer substations - Group 1

comment.narrative: <p>The commissioned capacity of transformer substations under Group 1 has slightly exceeded the revised target of 2 010 000 KVA. The incremental capacity was measured from the additional substation capacity through the procurement / installation of power transformers financed by the loan.</p>

title.narrative: Growth in electricity sales in project areas for Group 2 in East Indonesia

comment.narrative: <p>The electricity sales in Group 2 in East Indonesia grew by 126.16 percent at the completion, slightly higher than the revised target of 120 percent. The target (initially set at 122.00 percent) was revised down to reflect a lower projected growth demand for electricity in the project area, partly due to a lower economic growth. The achieved growth, nevertheless, is still slightly higher than the original target. The additional substations capacity has contributed to the increase of customers number and electricity sales, though it could not claim a full attribution to those increases, since external factors beyond the project boundary may have major role. The project partly attributed to this achievement.</p>

title.narrative: Growth in electricity sales in project areas for Group 2 in Java-Bali

comment.narrative: <p>The electricity sales in Group 2 (in Java-Bali) grew by 136.41 percent at the completion, higher than the revised target of 120 percent. This is nearly 16 percent higher than expected. The target (initially set at 135 percent) was revised down to reflect a lower projected growth demand for electricity in the project area, partly due to a lower economic growth. The achieved growth, nevertheless, is still higher than the original target as project areas have experienced relatively faster economic growth than Group 1. Included in the Group 2 are economically strong performing areas such as Jakarta, Central and East Java. The additional substations capacity has contributed to the increase of customers number and electricity sales, though it could not claim a full attribution to those increases, since external factors beyond the project boundary may have major role. The project partly attributed to this achievement.</p>

title.narrative: Growth in electricity sales in project areas for Group 2 in West Indonesia

comment.narrative: <p>The electricity sales in Group 2 in West Indonesia grew by 151.95 percent at the completion, slightly higher than the revised target of 120 percent. The target (initially set at 108.00 percent) was revised up to reflect a higher projected growth demand for electricity in the project area. The achieved growth, nevertheless, is still higher than the original target. The additional substations capacity has contributed to the increase of customers number and electricity sales, though it could not claim a full attribution to those increases, since external factors beyond the project boundary may have major role. The project partly attributed to this achievement.</p>

title.narrative: Electricity Sales in project areas for Group 1

comment.narrative: <p>The electricity sales in Group 1 increased to 14,108.77 GWh against 16,000 GWh targeted, a 10 percent lower than the revised target. The target (initially set at 18 580 GWh) was revised down to reflect a lower projected growth demand for electricity in the project area, partly due to a lower economic growth.  Another possible reason for lower than expected electricity sales could be that the driver of economic growth came mostly from agricultural and service sectors, which are commonly less energy intensive than the industrial sector.</p>

title.narrative: Progress in Procurement and Contract Completion - Group 1

comment.narrative: <p>Procurement and contract have been fully completed.</p>

title.narrative: Progress in Procurement and Contract Completion - Group 2

comment.narrative: <p>Procurement and contract have been fully completed.</p>

title.narrative: Commissioned capacity of transformer substations - Group 2

comment.narrative: <p>The commissioned capacity of transformer substations under Group 2 has been lower than the revised target as the processes have been hampered by challenging land procurement processes. The incremental capacity was measured from the additional substation capacity through the procurement / installation of power transformers financed by the loan.</p>
